residual: P2: radiusNoCeiling requires BOTH ceilings to be null, so a HALF-mistyped config still produces the exact false-success claim defect (3) was raised to eliminate. With `max_rewrite_ratio: "0.5"` (string -> radiusNum -> null) and `max_touched_existing_files: 8`, a plan declaring rewrite_ratio 0.99 / touched_existing_files 2 is reported as `state: 'WITHIN'` with `reason: 'every declared number is at or under its ceiling'` — but 0.99 was never compared against anything, because radiusBreaches short-circuits on `max !== null`. The declared number is neither under a ceiling nor reported as uncompared. The mitigation is real but partial: `thresholds` in the payload does carry `max_rewrite_ratio: null`, so a reader of events.jsonl can derive it — the WITHIN *reason string* is what overclaims. The plan explicitly chose this shape and pins it with a test ('one usable ceiling out of two is still a usable configuration'), so this is flagged for the human rather than as a plan violation; the implementer raised the same point as 'the mirror of the defect being fixed'.

P3: Switching `answered` from key-presence to answer-truthiness means a controller that writes an empty/null answer permanently consumes a round number without disarming the halt: escRound counts KEYS, so `{"s1:refactor-scope": ""}` re-raises as `s1:refactor-scope:2`, and a controller that keeps writing blanks mints an unbounded sequence of new escalation records (there is no round cap anywhere). This is the intended direction of the fix and matches the resolveCouncilObjection precedent (`if (latestAnswer(slice.id, 'council-objection')) return { plan }`), which has the same property today, so it is not a regression this diff introduces in isolation — but the previous behaviour terminated and this one does not. Verified by reading escRound/escId/latestAnswer: latestAnswer ranks the bare key as round 1 and returns only the NEWEST round's value, so a truthy round-2 answer does disarm correctly.
